title: Welch two-sample t test
biology: Evolutionary biologists compare adult beetle body length from two rearing environments.
design: Independent beetles assigned to cool or warm rearing; each beetle measured once.
question: Do mean body lengths differ between cool and warm environments?
null: The two population means are equal.
options: Factor order defines the reported difference
Use a paired test only for genuine pairs
assumptions: No severe outliers; check small samples closely
Groups need not share a variance
parametric: A scientifically sensible transformation may reduce strong skew
nonparametric: Rank-sum tests distributions; it is not a general test of means
A bootstrap interval can retain the mean-difference target

plot_args.note: Use a color for each group
Add group means with a distinct symbol

practice: If the Warm group is more variable, do you need ranks to test a mean difference?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1102)
d <- data.frame(environment = rep(c("Cool", "Warm"), c(26, 30)),
                length_mm = c(rnorm(26, 10, .65), rnorm(30, 10.7, 1.15)))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
beeswarm(length_mm ~ environment, data = d, pch = 21,
         bg = c("#246A73", "#B7663E"), col = "white", cex = 1.3,
         xlab = "Rearing environment", ylab = "Adult body length (mm)")
points(1:2, tapply(d$length_mm, d$environment, mean), pch = 18, cex = 2)
legend("topleft", "Group mean", pch = 18, bty = "n")
code_analysis:
d$environment <- factor(d$environment, levels = c("Cool", "Warm"))
fit <- t.test(length_mm ~ environment, data = d,
              var.equal = FALSE, conf.level = .95)
difference <- mean(d$length_mm[d$environment == "Cool"]) -
              mean(d$length_mm[d$environment == "Warm"])
generating_model: 26 independent Cool lengths come from Normal(10, 0.65 SD), and 30 independent Warm lengths from Normal(10.7, 1.15 SD).
generating_truth: The true Cool minus Warm mean difference is -0.7 mm. Variances differ (0.4225 versus 1.3225 mm squared).
teaching_point: Welch answers the equal-means question while allowing unequal group variances.
